abstract: We study nine-coloring extensions over an induced nine-chromatic vertex-critical core $Q$ in a biplanar graph, with Euler deficit $D(Q)=6|V(Q)|-12-e(Q)$. We prove that an exterior satisfying $e(F[X])\le2|X|-1$ for every nonempty vertex set $X$ always extends to some nine-coloring when $|V(Q)|\le15$ and $D(Q)\le9$. The exterior order is unrestricted. This covers fifteen-vertex, 69-edge critical cores and complements the retained theorem at core order at most seventeen and deficit at most eight. A minimal bad exterior has six through eight vertices. Zero-excess cases admit degree-list or leaf-clique repairs. The remaining cases have 805 direct positive graph-polynomial certificates, five certificates after a singleton core-color repair, and two instances of an elementary adjacent-pair list lemma. A standalone standard-library verifier independently checks all 810 coefficients and complete coverage of 187,452 labeled sparse graphs. The theorem imports the accepted order-twenty result. We also retain the separate hand theorem for arboricity-three exteriors at deficit at most five, with unrestricted core order. These results choose the core coloring; they neither extend every prescribed coloring nor assert that an arbitrary counterexample contains such a core or sparse exterior. The Earth–Moon problem remains open.

change_summary: Adds Theorem5 and Section12: induced nine-critical core order<=15 and deficit<=9 with arbitrary (2,1)-sparse exterior implies nine-colorability. Retains Theorems1/4 and their proofs. New proof reduces to6–8exterior vertices, uses leaf/singleton repairs and an adjacent-pair list lemma, plus810 positive coefficients with exhaustive187452labeledgraph coverage. Adds deficit9 supplement directory; preserves all five old supplement files byte for byte. No q16/17 deficit-nine, all-extension, or global Earth–Moon claim. Coauthor attribution for earlier joint work retained; new section developed and independently computationally checked by earth_moon_codex_two.
